findings.passage: That same year OpenAI's founders fought [Elon Musk](/personality-analysis/elon-musk), a co-founder and the lab's main early funder, over a for-profit arm and who would control it
findings.problem: The previous section ends in 2018–2019 (the November 2018 restart, the November 2019 wedding, the 2019 essay), so 'That same year' reads as 2019. The fight over the for-profit arm and control was in 2017 (S35: 'by 2017 ... Musk wanted control'; S12: September 2017). Two sentences later, 'Brockman's diary from that year' inherits the ambiguity.
findings.acceptance_test: The section opens with an absolute date ('In 2017, OpenAI's founders fought ...'), and 'from that year' unambiguously means 2017.

findings.passage: His moral vocabulary is the strongest evidence, and it applies to his own conduct: a private 2017 diary entry calling an option he and his co-founders were weighing "pretty morally bankrupt," and his verdict on the day he quit OpenAI, "It just wasn't right."
findings.problem: In the Type 1 FAQ, the list after 'applies to his own conduct' includes 'It just wasn't right', which judged the board's action on November 17, 2023 (S24), not his own conduct. The body states this accurately ('when he judges conduct, his own included'). The FAQ, which surfaces out of context, blurs it.
findings.acceptance_test: The FAQ either says the vocabulary judges conduct, 'his own included', or presents the diary entry as the self-directed example and the November 17 verdict as a judgment of others.

findings.passage: Whether these were one chatbot or two, AI was "definitely my life goal," as he told Altman in 2015.
findings.problem: S03 reads: 'I replied that AI was top of my list (and it was definitely my life goal).' The parenthetical may be his aside to blog readers rather than words said to Altman, so 'as he told Altman' is a plausible but uncertain reading (C142).
findings.acceptance_test: The attribution matches the source's form, e.g. 'AI was, he wrote in 2016, "definitely my life goal"', or the full sentence is quoted so the reader can see the parenthetical.

findings.problem: In the cited NPR report (S35), the appeal announcement comes from Musk's lawyer, Marc Toberoff ('I can sum it up in one word: appeal'). Musk's own quoted post says the merits were not reached. C165 carries the same attribution.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence reads 'Musk's lawyer said they would appeal' (or equivalent), or cites a source in which Musk himself announces the appeal. C165 matches.

findings.passage: Brockman, born in 1987 and raised in North Dakota
findings.problem: The article text is correct, but claim C01's text says 'Forbes listed him as 38 in September 2026'. The Forbes list (S30) gives 'Greg Brockman, 37'. This is an evidence-record inaccuracy.
findings.acceptance_test: C01's claim text matches S30 (37), or drops the Forbes age.

findings.passage: At Stripe he found "a repeatable pattern for creating software systems from nothing: focus single-mindedly on the software, shutting out all distractions and working from wake until sleep."
findings.problem: The quotation closes with a period where S04's sentence continues ', which would inspire others to contribute their best work (importantly, measured by output quality rather than hours).' The meaning is not reversed, but the omitted clause (inspiring others; measuring by output quality) bears on the article's own Three-versus-One test.
findings.acceptance_test: The trim is marked (closing the quotation without a terminal period inside, or with an ellipsis), or the clause is quoted and weighed in the type argument.

findings.passage: So the Three reading leads on how he scores his work and the One on how he judges conduct: a medium-confidence call that would flip if new first-person evidence showed him scoring his own work mainly on whether it was right.
findings.problem: The type case is honest but split by domain. The costliest choice in the record (November 17, 2023) is conceded to One or Six. The Three side of the work-scoring test rests on small self-presentational asides (the Kaggle parenthetical, Goodfellow being impressed, 'validating') that the article concedes a One could share, while the 2019 essay's correctness frustrations show a rightness standard applied to his own work. The One alternative is weakened, not failed. This is why the Enneagram dimension scores below the release floor. It is not a wording defect, and manufacturing certainty would be worse.
findings.acceptance_test: On refresh, either (a) a sourced first-person or named-colleague observation is added that the One reading fails, such as a dated case where he narrates or chooses the visible result over correctness in his own work at a real cost, with confidence language adjusted only as far as that evidence supports; or (b) the call stays at medium confidence and the page holds until such evidence exists.
